16:04:23  john@framie  ~/c/d/g/j/a/main  main ≢   (nix-impure) podman pull ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:0.0.21
Trying to pull ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest...
Trying to pull ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:0.0.21...
Error: unable to copy from source docker://ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest: initializing source docker://ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest: unable to retrieve auth token: [REDACTED] username/password: [REDACTED]
Error: unable to copy from source docker://ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:0.0.21: initializing source docker://ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:0.0.21: unable to retrieve auth token: [REDACTED] username/password: [REDACTED]

How can I auth to ghcr.io? `podman login` and then which user/pass?

Use your GitHub username and a GitHub personal access token (PAT), not your GitHub password:

```bash
export CR_PAT="$(< [REDACTED SECRET PATH])"
printf '%s' "$CR_PAT" |
  podman login ghcr.io \
    --username johnrichardrinehart \
    --password-stdin
unset CR_PAT
```

Then pull each image separately:

```bash
podman pull ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:latest
podman pull ghcr.io/johnrichardrinehart/agent-sandbox:0.0.21
```

The token needs:

- `read:packages` to pull private images.
- Repository access if the package inherits access from a private repository.
- SSO authorization if the package belongs to an organization that enforces SSO.

If cached credentials are wrong:

```bash
podman logout ghcr.io
printf '%s' "$(< [REDACTED SECRET PATH])" |
  podman login ghcr.io -u johnrichardrinehart --password-stdin
```

Also, `podman pull IMAGE1 IMAGE2` treats both arguments as separate images, as shown by your output. Explicit tags are clearer.
